chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) urged us to perform the Friday prayer until I thought he meant for us to come to him. So I said to him, 'We will visit you in the morning.' He said, 'No, I meant [the prayer] at your place.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq mean when he urged the companions to perform Friday prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that his intense emphasis on Friday prayer was not an invitation for private audiences, but a directive to prioritize congregational worship (*Jama'ah*) in their local communities. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly view that the communal aspect of Jumu'ah is central to its spiritual and social efficacy, rather than merely seeking the Imam's personal presence. It reflects the broader tradition of maintaining communal identity and religious practice even in the absence of the Imam.
